Common questions

About Fere AI

Fere AI is an AI-powered crypto trading and research platform that gives traders autonomous agents with non-custodial wallets to analyze markets and execute on-chain trades around the clock. It runs in the web app or inside ChatGPT and Claude via MCP.

Turning a sentence into a trading strategy

Describe what you want to watch or trade in plain English. Fere compiles that description into readable rules you can inspect before anything runs, then executes them on a schedule — paper trading first, with hard position caps and a one-tap kill switch.

Supported chains and venues

Scheduled strategies run on Solana, Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, BNB Chain, Polygon, and Hyperliquid. Fere also supports Polymarket prediction markets.

Custody of your funds

Each agent gets its own non-custodial wallet, so you keep custody of the funds. Fere AI does not offer a fiat on-ramp.

Using Fere inside ChatGPT or Claude

Fere exposes a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server at https://api.fereai.xyz/mcp, so any MCP client — including ChatGPT and Claude — can research markets and place trades through it.

Pricing

Lite is $9 per month (1,100 credits), Pro is $29 per month (4,200 credits), and Whale is $99 per month (16,000 credits). Annual billing is two months free compared with paying monthly.

Create your new account

Set up a Polymarket account. Fireplace runs on the same Polymarket markets, so your positions carry over.

Polymarket

Cancel your open orders

Resting limit orders lock up your cash and shares — cancel them so everything is free to migrate, and nothing fills after you've left.

No open orders — nothing to cancel.
3

Migrate your positions + cash

In Polymarket, open your profile and use Copy address (NOT the Deposit address) — that wallet holds your positions and balance. Paste it here and hit Migrate. This moves ALL of your open positions AND your entire cash balance to it in one step. We sign the on-chain transfer; your private key never leaves Fireplace. It's on-chain and can't be undone, so double-check the address.

Need help? Reach out to support before the deadline — we can't assist once the app is offline.

Stablecoins make all of this cleaner. When capital stays dollar-denominated, agents focus purely on yield optimization without managing currency exposure. No hedging ETH volatility. No calculating real returns against price movements. Just maximizing dollar-denominated yield within user-defined risk parameters.

The barrier to deploying these agents used to be technical skill. Building autonomous systems required code, smart contract knowledge, and infrastructure most users couldn't access. Fraction AI removed that barrier. Users deposit stablecoins into Stable-Up vaults, describe their goals (risk tolerance, target returns, constraints on protocol exposure), and AI agents handle allocations across dozens of integrated protocols including Moonwell, Silo, Morpho, Yearn, Euler, and Avantis, analyzing opportunities across multiple chains while executing on Base.

120,000 users have deployed 160,000 agents this way, generating 3.5 million sessions. Most created their agents using natural language, describing what they wanted rather than writing code to get it. APYs range from 6-20% depending on agent configuration and market conditions.

## The Efficiency Gap Is Closing

The infrastructure worked and the yields existed, but the human limitations prevented capture.

AI agents remove those limitations. They monitor continuously, execute without emotion, and optimize across more protocols than any human could track. Yields that went uncaptured start compounding. Liquidations that would have extracted value get avoided. Gas costs that would have accumulated get optimized.

Stablecoins complete the picture by providing stable, dollar-denominated capital that agents can optimize without managing currency volatility. The focus becomes pure yield capture within user-defined risk parameters.

Bloomberg Intelligence projects stablecoin flows reaching $56 trillion by 2030. As capital in the system grows, the efficiency gap between optimized and unoptimized management grows proportionally. The cost of staying manual keeps rising.11:T1ea3,400 million people own crypto. 7 million use DeFi. That's a mere 1.5% penetration rate, and it has nothing to do with technology.

The numbers are brutal. 89% of newcomers leave DeFi protocols within the first 5 minutes (ICODA Research). Not hours. Minutes. 67% experience transaction failures from hidden fees they didn't understand. Only 17% feel confident using DeFi tools at all.

The technology works fine. Protocols have deep liquidity, fast settlement, and real yields. The interface is what's broken.

DeFi was built by developers for developers. The result: a system that punishes anyone who doesn't already understand it.

Meanwhile, stablecoin infrastructure scales to $33 trillion in annual volume (Artemis Analytics). Layer 2s drop transaction costs to fractions of a cent. New yield opportunities launch daily across hundreds of protocols.

The opportunity is massive. The door is just too hard to open.

## What's Actually Broken

DeFi's interface problem runs deeper than ugly dashboards.

Start with the jargon. Slippage. Impermanent loss. Collateralization ratio. Liquidation threshold. Health factor. These terms mean nothing to someone who just wants their money to earn more than a savings account. According to WunderTrading, 60% of cryptocurrency holders don't understand blockchain technology or DeFi at all.

Then there's the process. Using a typical DeFi protocol means connecting a wallet, navigating to the right page, selecting the right asset, setting parameters you may not understand, approving a contract interaction, confirming a transaction, paying gas in a token you need to already hold, and then manually monitoring your position going forward. Miss one step, set one parameter wrong, and you lose money with no recourse.

The stakes make it worse. There's no "forgot password" in DeFi. No customer support to reverse a bad transaction. One wrong address, one misplaced decimal, one unnoticed liquidation threshold, and capital vanishes permanently.

Compare this to traditional finance. Open a savings account in five minutes. Deposit money. Earn interest. Done. No jargon, no multi-step processes, no risk of catastrophic user error.

DeFi offers better yields, more transparency, and actual ownership of assets. But it demands users learn an entirely new language and navigate an interface designed for engineers. The 98.5% who stay away aren't irrational. They're responding to a system that punishes newcomers.

## The Opportunity Explosion Nobody Can Capture

While users struggle with interfaces, the opportunity set keeps expanding.

New protocols launch weekly. Yield sources multiply across Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, Optimism, Solana, and dozens of other chains. Stablecoin lending rates shift hourly across Aave, Compound, Morpho, Euler, and newer entrants. Liquidity mining programs start and end constantly. The DeFi landscape that was complex in 2021 has become an order of magnitude more fragmented.

Capturing optimal returns now requires monitoring hundreds of venues simultaneously. When Morpho offers 8% on USDC while Aave sits at 5%, the user who notices and moves first captures the spread. When a new incentive program launches on Base, early depositors earn outsized rewards. When rates normalize, capital needs to rotate again.

Humans can't do this. According to McKinsey's analysis of DeFi payments infrastructure, stablecoins facilitate $20-30 billion in real on-chain payments daily across an increasingly complex web of protocols. Tracking yield shifts across this landscape requires attention no individual can sustain.

The math gets worse over time. As DeFi matures, alpha comes from speed and coverage. The user manually checking three protocols loses to the system monitoring three hundred. The gap between available yield and captured yield widens every month.

## Natural Language Changes Everything

The interface breakthrough came from an unexpected direction: just let people talk.

Traditional DeFi requires users to learn the system's language. Natural language interfaces flip this. The system learns to understand users instead.

Describe what you want: "Put my stablecoins to work earning yield, keep risk moderate, don't lock anything for more than a week." The AI parses intent, identifies constraints, and builds a strategy that fits. No jargon required. No multi-step processes. No parameter tuning.

Fraction AI built this into their core product. Users create agents by describing goals in sentences, not code. 120,000 users have done exactly that, deploying over 160,000 agents across 3.5 million sessions.

Stable-Up applies this specifically to stablecoin management. Deposit USDC or other stablecoins, describe your risk tolerance and goals, and AI agents handle allocation across dozens of integrated protocols including Moonwell, Silo, Morpho, Yearn, Euler, and Avantis. The agents analyze opportunities across multiple chains while executing on Base, delivering 6-20% APY depending on strategy parameters.

The user who couldn't explain "impermanent loss" can still access sophisticated yield optimization. The complexity doesn't disappear. It moves behind the interface.

Stablecoins amplify the effect. When everything denominates in dollars, users think in terms they already understand. No mental math converting ETH prices. No wondering if token volatility ate the yield. Just "I put in $10,000, now I have $10,600." Clean, comprehensible and familiar.

## The Bigger Picture: Programmable Treasury

What works for individual users scales to businesses.

Circle, Stripe, and Fireblocks now offer programmable treasury capabilities. Companies can issue stablecoin budgets to AI agents with embedded controls: daily limits, transaction caps, approved counterparties. The agent operates autonomously within defined boundaries.

The x402 protocol accelerates this by embedding stablecoin payments directly into HTTP requests. AI agents can pay for APIs, compute resources, and services without requiring account setup, subscription management, or manual approval flows. When an agent needs data from a paid service, it pays automatically and continues operating. Google launched the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) in September 2025, building on x402 to standardize how agents transact.

Imagine a procurement system that receives a restock signal, evaluates supplier options, negotiates terms, and settles payment entirely on its own. Not by accessing the general ledger, but by operating within a defined stablecoin allocation governed by programmable constraints. Platforms are piloting these workflows now.

The shift from "human approves every transaction" to "human sets rules, agent executes" changes how organizations manage capital. Treasury operations become programmable. Spending becomes auditable by default. Execution becomes continuous rather than batched.

## The Door Is Finally Opening

The technology was never the problem. DeFi protocols have offered superior yields, transparency, and ownership for years. The interface kept people out, demanding technical knowledge and constant attention that most users couldn't provide.

Natural language changes the access equation. Users describe goals instead of configuring parameters. AI agents handle execution, monitoring, and optimization. Stablecoins simplify the mental model by keeping everything denominated in dollars.

The opportunity set in DeFi keeps expanding. New protocols, new chains, new yield sources launch constantly. Capturing optimal returns requires real-time monitoring across an increasingly fragmented landscape. Manual users can't keep up. Agent-assisted users don't have to.

The 98.5% of crypto holders who never touched DeFi weren't making an irrational choice. They were responding to an interface that punished newcomers. That interface is being rebuilt.

Something shifted in Q4 2024. The AI agent sector exploded from $4.8 billion to $15.5 billion in market cap within three months (Nansen). By early 2025, the broader AI crypto market crossed $50 billion. Investors noticed, pouring $516 million into AI crypto projects in the first eight months of 2025 alone, a 6% jump from all of 2024.

Meanwhile, stablecoins were having their own moment. Transaction volume grew 72% year-over-year. USDC processed $18.3 trillion. USDT handled $13.3 trillion. Monthly volumes hit $1.25 trillion in September, approaching the scale of traditional payment rails like ACH.

The two trends are feeding each other.

AI agents need money that moves like they do: instantly, globally, without permission slips. Stablecoins are the only financial infrastructure that fits. No bank accounts required. No business hours. No geographic restrictions. Just programmable dollars moving at the speed of code.

## Why AI Agents Need Stablecoins

Traditional finance has no idea what to do with autonomous systems.

Banks require human or corporate entities behind every account. Credit cards need manual approvals. Payment processors demand identity verification, business registration, compliance paperwork. The entire infrastructure assumes a human is making decisions.

AI agents break that assumption. They operate continuously, make decisions autonomously, and need to move value without waiting for someone to click "approve." Traditional rails can't serve them, not because of technical limitations, but because the whole model assumes human involvement at every step.

Stablecoins solve this by removing the gatekeeper

Galaxy Digital's Michael Novogratz put it directly in a Bloomberg interview: "In the not-so-distant future, the biggest user of stablecoins is going to be AI."

Since launch, x402 on Solana alone has processed over 35 million transactions and $10 million in volume.

Stablecoins give AI agents what traditional finance can't: economic autonomy.

## Early Attempts and Their Limits

The idea of AI agents managing capital on-chain has been around for a while. Some projects have made real progress.

Giza Protocol's ARMA agents have executed over 100,000 autonomous trades, optimizing more than $30 million in capital with zero human oversight. Olas Network processes over 700,000 transactions monthly, with agents handling the majority of Safe transactions on Gnosis Chain during peak days. These systems prove the concept works.

The limitation is accessibility. Most existing platforms require users to write code, understand smart contract architecture, or navigate complex technical setups. Giza targets developers building custom strategies. Olas requires understanding of agent frameworks and deployment processes. The average user who wants their stablecoins working harder has no entry point.

There's also the strategy constraint. Many early agent systems lock users into predefined approaches. You pick from a menu of existing strategies rather than defining your own parameters. Customization requires technical skills, which brings you back to the coding barrier.

The result: AI agents managing capital exist, but access remains limited to technical users and predefined playbooks. The infrastructure proved the model while the interface kept most people out.

## Making It Accessible

Fraction AI took a different approach: remove the technical barrier entirely.

Users don't write code. They don't configure smart contracts. They don't need to understand agent frameworks or deployment infrastructure. They describe what they want in plain English.

"Maximize yield on my USDC while keeping risk low." "Rebalance between lending protocols when rates shift by more than 2%." "Exit positions if volatility spikes above my threshold."

The AI interprets the intent and builds an agent that executes it. The agent then monitors markets continuously, tracks opportunities across dozens of integrated protocols, and adjusts positions based on the parameters the user defined.

No coding. No technical setup. No 3 AM monitoring. Users describe outcomes, agents deliver execution.

The shift mirrors what happened in other industries. Website building moved from requiring developers to drag-and-drop tools. Video editing moved from professional studios to mobile apps. Now capital management is making the same transition, from technical skill requirement to accessible interface.

Stablecoins provide the foundation. AI agents provide the execution. Natural language provides the access. The combination opens autonomous yield optimization to anyone who can describe what they want.

The building blocks for an agent-driven economy exist today.

Stablecoins provide programmable, permissionless money that moves at the speed agents require. Protocols like x402 enable agent-to-agent payments without human involvement. title: px_kairos_trade_home.raw — part 10/23
body:
runs on, exposed directly. REST and WebSocket, documented, with the aggregation already done.

Snapshot what you need on request, stream what you need continuously, over documented endpoints.

The cross-venue view is what you call — one integration instead of one per platform.

Kairos finds the best bid and best offer for a trade in prediction markets by merging every venue's book into a single ladder, then quoting the top of it. No one exchange holds both sides of the touch, so the composite spread is tighter than any venue's own — and an order sent to the NBBO endpoint routes to whichever venue is actually showing that price.

Scoped keys, published rate limits and a sandbox to build against before you go live.

Settlement, wallets, liquidity, blockchain — all running before you finish setup. Your market is live in under 15 minutes with no code.

FREE · NO CODE · LIVE IN 15 MINUTES
Everything already built

The full stack. Ready to go live.

From the trading engine to your leaderboard, every feature you’d expect from a trading platform is already running. You just add your brand.

Your domain. Your brand. Any language.
Custom domain, logo, colors, and UI language. Available in English, Portuguese, Spanish, German, French, Japanese, Chinese, Arabic, Russian, Italian, and Polish out of the box.
Shared liquidity from day one.
Mirror active Polymarket markets with built-in order flow. Your site feels live the moment it launches — no cold start, no empty order books.
Leaderboard + PnL built in.
Trader rankings, profit and loss tracking, and activity feeds are live by default. Your community has a reason to keep coming back.
On-chain affiliate system.
Let others promote your market and earn a share of fees — settled trustlessly on-chain. No manual payouts, no spreadsheets.
Bot SDKs for automated trading.
Python and Rust SDKs let market makers and power users run bots directly on your platform — increasing volume and depth automatically.
OpenZeppelin-audited contracts.
Smart contracts derived from Polymarket's architecture. UMA-based resolution for transparent, verifiable market settlement. You don't need to know any of this — it just works.

This is what your site will look like.

This is a functional demo with mirrored Polymarket markets. Explore it, trade on it, and imagine it with your brand, your audience, and your questions.

demo.kuest.comLive Demo

Ready to turn your audience into a revenue stream?

Launch my market — it's free

FAQ

How long does it take, and do I need technical skills?
Most markets go live in under 15 minutes. You launch from /launch with a guided setup — no code, no contract deployment, no DevOps. If you can set up a Shopify store, you can launch a Kuest market.
Can I show Polymarket markets on my site?
Yes. You can mirror active markets from Polymarket — either all categories or only the ones relevant to your niche (crypto, sports, politics, etc.). These mirrored markets come with shared liquidity from day one, so your site feels live from the moment it's published.
Can I create my own markets? Who provides the liquidity?
Yes. You can create custom markets around any question you choose. Mirrored Polymarket markets have shared liquidity built in. Markets you create yourself depend on your audience trading — so your own content and community drive the volume there. You can also opt into cross-market liquidity sharing for creator markets.
How do I make money, and can I set my own fees?
You set a trading fee rate on your market — typically between 0.5% and 3%. Every time someone trades, that fee goes directly to your wallet. No revenue share, no intermediary, no waiting. You control the rate and can change it at any time.
Can I use my own domain and branding?
Yes. You can launch with your own domain, logo, colors, and category structure so the market feels entirely native to your brand — not a Kuest white-label.
How are markets resolved?
Kuest uses UMA-based resolution rails for transparent, verifiable settlement. The smart contracts are derived from Polymarket's — audited by OpenZeppelin — and adapted to support shared liquidity across markets. You don't need to understand any of this to use it, but it means the financial infrastructure under your market is the same stack that's processed billions in volume.
Is there a cost to launch?
The creator launch flow is free to start. Production infrastructure pricing is usage-based — you pay when you scale, not before. Enterprise plans start at $100K.
Can I self-host Kuest?
The codebase is open source under the Kuest MIT+Commons license. Forks for branding, frontend changes, and custom UX are welcome. Production deployments, however, must use Kuest infrastructure. Running an independent trading stack requires a separate commercial agreement.

<style>
  :root {
    --bg: #111319;
    --bg-2: #161922;
    --ink: #ffffff;
    --ink-dim: #adb0b9;
    --ink-mute: #6b6f7a;
    --line: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.06);
    --line-strong: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.11);
    --moby: #30e0a1;
    --moby-deep: #21ce99;
    --moby-soft: rgba(48, 224, 161, 0.10);
    --moby-glow: rgba(48, 224, 161, 0.35);
    --sans: "Mona Sans", -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Proxima Nova", Arial, sans-serif;
    --mono: "JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace, monospace;
  }

  * { box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0; padding: 0; }

  html, body {
    background: var(--bg);
    color: var(--ink);
    font-family: var(--sans);
    -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;
    -moz-osx-font-smoothing: grayscale;
    overflow-x: hidden;
  }

  body {
    min-height: 100vh;
    position: relative;
    background:
      radial-gradient(ellipse 45% 30% at 50% 0%, rgba(48, 224, 161, 0.08), transparent 70%),
      radial-gradient(ellipse 40% 30% at 100% 100%, rgba(48, 224, 161, 0.04), transparent 70%),
      var(--bg);
  }

  body::after {
    content: "";
    position: fixed;
    inset: 0;
    pointer-events: none;
    z-index: 0;
    background-image:
      linear-gradient(to right, var(--line) 1px, transparent 1px),
      linear-gradient(to bottom, var(--line) 1px, transparent 1px);
    background-size: 88px 88px;
    mask-image: radial-gradient(ellipse 70% 60% at 50% 40%, black 20%, transparent 75%);
    -webkit-mask-image: radial-gradient(ellipse 70% 60% at 50% 40%, black 20%, transparent 75%);
    opacity: 0.5;
  }

  .container {
    position: relative;
    z-index: 2;
    max-width: 1120px;
    margin: 0 auto;
    padding: 32px 40px 80px;
  }

  /* ===== HEADER ===== */
  header {
    display: flex;
    align-items: center;
    justify-content: space-between;
    padding-bottom: 88px;
    animation: fadeDown 0.7s ease-out;
  }

  .wordmark {
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: center;
    text-decoration: none;
    line-height: 0;
  }

  .wordmark img {
    height: 28px;
    width: auto;
    display: block;
  }

  .status-pill {
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: 8px;
    padding: 7px 13px;
    border: 1px solid var(--line-strong);
    border-radius: 100px;
    font-family: var(--mono);
    font-size: 11px;
    letter-spacing: 0.04em;
    color: var(--ink-dim);
    background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.02);
  }

  .status-dot {
    width: 6px;
    height: 6px;
    border-radius: 50%;
    background: var(--moby);
    box-shadow: 0 0 8px var(--moby-glow);
    animation: pulse 2s ease-in-out infinite;
  }

  @keyframes pulse {
    0%, 100% { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1); }
    50% { opacity: 0.55; transform: scale(0.8); }
  }

  /* ===== HERO ===== */
  .hero {
    max-width: 760px;
    margin: 0 auto 96px;
    text-align: center;
    animation: fadeUp 0.85s ease-out 0.1s both;
  }

  .eyebrow {
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: 8px;
    font-family: var(--mono);
    font-size: 11px;
    letter-spacing: 0.16em;
    text-transform: uppercase;
    color: var(--moby);
    margin-bottom: 32px;
  }

  .eyebrow-dot {
    display: inline-block;
    width: 5px;
    height: 5px;
    background: var(--moby);
    border-radius: 50%;
    box-shadow: 0 0 8px var(--moby-glow);
  }

  h1 {
    font-family: var(--sans);
    font-weight: 600;
    font-size: clamp(34px, 4.4vw, 56px);
    line-height: 1.08;
    letter-spacing: -0.028em;
    margin-bottom: 22px;
    color: var(--ink);
  }

  h1 .accent {
    color: var(--moby);
  }

  .lede {
    max-width: 520px;
    margin: 0 auto;
    font-size: 17px;
    line-height: 1.55;
    color: var(--ink-dim);
    font-weight: 400;
  }

  .lede a {
    color: var(--ink);
    text-decoration: none;
    border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line-strong);
    transition: border-color 0.2s;
  }

  .lede a:hover { border-color: var(--moby); }

  /* ===== TILES ===== */
  .tiles {
    display: grid;
    grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr;
    gap: 18px;
    margin-bottom: 80px;
  }

  .tile {
    position: relative;
    padding: 36px;
    border: 1px solid var(--line-strong);
    border-radius: 18px;
    background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.022), rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.004));
    overflow: hidden;
    display: flex;
    flex-direction: column;
    min-height: 360px;
    text-decoration: none;
    color: inherit;
    transition: transform 0.4s cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1), border-color 0.4s ease;
    animation: fadeUp 0.95s ease-out both;
  }

  .tile:nth-child(1) { animation-delay: 0.25s; }
  .tile:nth-child(2) { animation-delay: 0.38s; }

  .tile::before {
    content: "";
    position: absolute;
    inset: 0;
    background: radial-gradient(circle at var(--mx, 50%) var(--my, 50%), var(--moby-soft), transparent 50%);
    opacity: 0;
    transition: opacity 0.4s ease;
    pointer-events: none;
  }

  .tile:hover {
    transform: translateY(-3px);
    border-color: rgba(48, 224, 161, 0.22);
  }

  .tile:hover::before { opacity: 1; }

  .tile-featured {
    border-color: rgba(48, 224, 161, 0.26);
    background:
      linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(48, 224, 161, 0.04), rgba(48, 224, 161, 0.005));
  }

  .tile-featured::after {
    content: "";
    position: absolute;
    top: 0;
    left: 10%;
    right: 10%;
    height: 1px;
    background: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent, var(--moby), transparent);
    opacity: 0.6;
  }

  .tile-label {
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: center;
    gap: 8px;
    font-family: var(--mono);
    font-size: 11px;
    letter-spacing: 0.12em;
    color: var(--ink-mute);
    text-transform: uppercase;
    margin-bottom: 28px;
  }

  .tile-label .dash {
    width: 18px;
    height: 1px;
    background: var(--ink-mute);
  }

  .tile-featured .tile-label {
    color: var(--moby);
  }
  .tile-featured .tile-label .dash {
    background: var(--moby);
  }

  .tile h2 {
    font-family: var(--sans);
    font-weight: 600;
    font-size: clamp(24px, 2.4vw, 30px);
    line-height: 1.15;
    letter-spacing: -0.022em;
    margin-bottom: 14px;
  }

  .tile h2 .accent { color: var(--moby); }

  .tile p {
    font-size: 15px;
    line-height: 1.6;
    color: var(--ink-dim);
    margin-bottom: 28px;
    max-width: 440px;
  }

  .tile-cta {
    margin-top: auto;
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: center;
    justify-content: space-between;
    width: 100%;
    padding: 15px 20px;
    border-radius: 10px;
    font-family: var(--sans);
    font-size: 14.5px;
    font-weight: 600;
    letter-spacing: -0.005em;
    text-decoration: none;
    transition: all 0.3s ease;
  }

  .cta-primary {
    background: var(--moby);
    color: #052418;
  }
  .cta-primary:hover {
    background: #3df0ad;
    box-shadow: 0 8px 28px -6px var(--moby-glow);
    transform: translateY(-1px);
  }

  .cta-secondary {
    background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.04);
    color: var(--ink);
    border: 1px solid var(--line-strong);
  }
  .cta-secondary:hover {
    background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.07);
    border-color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.2);
  }

  .cta-arrow {
    display: inline-flex;
    align-items: center;
    transition: transform 0.3s ease;
  }
  .tile-cta:hover .cta-arrow { transform: translateX(3px); }
  .cta-arrow svg { width: 16px; height: 16px; }

  .tile-note {
    margin-top: 12px;
    font-family: var(--mono);
    font-size: 11px;
    letter-spacing: 0.04em;
    color: var(--ink-mute);
    text-align: center;
  }

  /* ===== FOOTER ===== */
  footer {
    border-top: 1px solid var(--line);
    padding-top: 26px;
    display: flex;
    justify-content: space-between;
    align-items: center;
    flex-wrap: wrap;
    gap: 16px;
    animation: fadeUp 1s ease-out 0.55s both;
  }

  .footer-copy {
    font-family: var(--mono);
    font-size: 11px;
    letter-spacing: 0.04em;
    color: var(--ink-mute);
  }
  .footer-copy .ink { color: var(--ink-dim); }

  .footer-links {
    display: flex;
    gap: 22px;
    font-family: var(--mono);
    font-size: 11px;
    letter-spacing: 0.04em;
  }
  .footer-links a {
    color: var(--ink-dim);
    text-decoration: none;
    transition: color 0.2s;
  }
  .footer-links a:hover { color: var(--moby); }

  /* ===== ANIMATIONS ===== */
  @keyframes fadeDown {
    from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-10px); }
    to { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); }
  }
  @keyframes fadeUp {
    from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(18px); }
    to { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); }
  }

How it works

The edge engine, end to end.

A single pipeline reads every market, models the probability, and tells you where the price disagrees.

  1. 01

    Read every market

    Octagon scrapes Kalshi's full universe, embeds it, and clusters it nightly into thematic and behavioral groups.

    GET /predictions/kalshi/markets · /clusters
  3. 02

    Model the probability

    Per-event research agents read sources, weigh drivers, and produce a model probability with confidence — every claim cited.

    GET /predictions/events
  5. 03

    Compare to live price

    Edge = model − market. Surfaced in Reports, the Live Edge feed, the News stream, and via a single API endpoint.

    GET /predictions/kalshi/markets-with-edge

Frequently Asked Questions

Get In Touch

How is Octagon different from Polymarket research or Kalshi's own platform?

+

Kalshi and Polymarket are exchanges — they show you the current price. Octagon is the intelligence layer on top: AI research agents generate an independent model probability for each event, every claim is cited to source, and the gap between our model and the live price is what we call edge. We expose that edge through Reports, a real-time News feed, a trading CLI, and typed REST APIs you can build on.

What is Octagon?

+

Octagon is an AI-powered market intelligence platform that integrates public and private market data in a single API. This site features our prediction market research, generating continuously updated reports on Kalshi markets. Each report covers a single market question, shows the current market probability alongside our model's estimated probability, and cites every claim to its source. Reports update automatically as new information becomes available.

How does Octagon work?

+

Octagon uses multi-agent AI systems that continuously track, analyze, and interpret millions of data points from public, private, and prediction markets. Our agents crawl news sources, financial filings, and market data in real time, then synthesize findings into research reports with cited sources. Reports update automatically as new information appears, so you always have the latest analysis without manual effort.

How do I access Kalshi prediction market research?

+

You can browse all research reports for free on this site. For API access, MCP integration, or higher usage limits, Octagon offers paid plans starting with a 15-day free trial. The Plus plan includes 200 research credits per month and the Pro plan includes 600 — both work with any OpenAI-compatible client or MCP-enabled IDE like Cursor or Claude Desktop.

What data coverage do you have?

+

We deploy AI agents to constantly crawl a broad range of data sources and validate information accuracy. Our comprehensive coverage includes:
Companies: 3M+ private and 8,000+ public equities
Funding & M&A Deals: 2M+ transactions tracked and analyzed
Investors & Funds: Detailed insights on 500k+ investors and 100k+ funds
People & Networks: Profiles of 4M+ influential professionals across markets

Who is behind Octagon?

+

Octagon is backed by AI Fund, an early-stage venture firm founded by Dr. Andrew Ng in 2017. AI Fund is backed by a $176M fund from top-tier investors and has incubated 33+ AI companies. The company also partners with SALT, whose events connect with over $15T of investible capital globally.

Market makers

  • Calibrate spreads and skew against full tick history.

Prop trading firms

  • Price divergence across venues arrives with fee and spread context attached.
  • One normalized WebSocket keyed by market covers every venue.

Hedge funds & macro research

Common Questions

Ostium is a decentralized perpetual futures exchange that lets you trade stocks, commodities, and forex with leverage — directly from your crypto wallet, with no broker or custodian.

With Ostium, you keep full custody of your funds. There are no account approvals, no frozen positions, no hidden spreads, and no intermediaries. Everything is settled on-chain via smart contracts.

Ostium offers deep liquidity across global markets — equities, gold, oil, forex — with transparent on-chain pricing tied to real-world data. You get institutional-grade markets with DeFi-grade access.

Just a crypto wallet (like MetaMask or Rabby) and USDC on Arbitrum. Connect your wallet at app.ostium.com and you can start trading in under a minute.

1970s-1980s: SOVIET "PIZZINT" DOCTRINE

Soviet intelligence operatives develop unconventional surveillance methodology targeting Washington D.C.'s late-night food delivery patterns. KGB codename: "PIZZINT" (Pizza Intelligence).

Operational Logic:

"If lights were burning late at the Pentagon or CIA, and delivery couriers were hauling stacks of pizzas through the door, something big might be brewing behind closed doors."

Strategic Rationale:

"When U.S. military and intelligence staff worked late into the night during emergencies, they would order large quantities of food—especially pizza—since it is quick and convenient. A spike in pizza orders could signal that something significant was happening behind closed doors."

1983

1983-1989: PATTERN VALIDATION PHASE

Local pizza delivery drivers began noticing they could anticipate "big news" 72 hours in advance by upticks in orders to government buildings. The pattern held across multiple military operations, as documented by TIME magazine in 1990.

Original Testimony

"We know. Absolutely. Pentagon orders doubled up the night before the Panama attack; same thing happened before the Grenada invasion. Last Wednesday, we got a lot of orders, starting around midnight. We figured something was up."

— Domino's Pizza Runner, TIME Magazine, August 13, 1990

Same pattern observed before Operation Just Cause

The most celebrated case came during the Gulf Crisis. Frank Meeks, owner of 43 D.C. Domino's franchises, documented unprecedented late-night deliveries as U.S. forces prepared to expel Iraqi troops from Kuwait.

PolyBot is a Telegram trading bot for Polymarket. It lets you trade prediction markets from Telegram with fast execution, copy trading, automated strategies, and risk controls.

Open PolyBot in Telegram, connect your Safe wallet, fund it with USDC, and place market or limit orders directly from chat. PolyBot keeps the trading workflow inside Telegram so you can react quickly without switching apps.

PolyBot is built around a Safe wallet setup you control. You keep access to your wallet, can export the owner key, and can withdraw funds whenever you choose.

PolyBot charges a transparent 1% flat fee on successful trades.

You can use PolyBot to trade Polymarket markets of any type.

PolyBot is built for fast execution. Market orders route immediately at the best available price, and limit orders trigger automatically once the market reaches your target. Funds settle after the on-chain confirmation.

Yes. PolyBot supports copy trading so you can follow selected wallets, set risk parameters, control sizing, and automate how trades are mirrored into your own portfolio.

Yes. You can build automated strategies for crypto up/down markets with trigger prices, take-profit rules, stop-loss protection, trailing stops, and entry windows that execute from Telegram.

Polymarket publishes CLOB APIs and client libraries for programmatic market data, orders, and trading workflows. Automation still has to follow the current platform terms, market rules, and geographic restrictions, and a bot does not remove the user’s responsibility for the orders it places.

No trading bot can guarantee profit. A bot executes a strategy faster and more consistently, but results still depend on the strategy, probability estimates, liquidity, spread, slippage, fees, position sizing, and risk management. Bad rules can automate losses just as efficiently as good rules automate execution.

Market orders execute instantly at the best available price - perfect when speed matters more than the exact price.

Limit orders let you choose your exact price - your order only fills when the market reaches it, giving you full control over your entry or exit price.

Copy Score is one number per trader: what following them has left over, after everything it costs to follow them. Free on every profile and every trade card.

Profit Is Not The Point

A trader can make money and still be a bad copy. You fill worse than they do, you pay venue fees, and you pay us. Copy Score subtracts all of it and asks what is left for you.

Challenges

Sound Familiar?

Too many traders, no way to know who’s good

Polymarket has thousands of traders. Most tools show you a leaderboard and leave you to guess. A big P&L tells you nothing about whether copying that trader would have paid you anything.

Copy Score answers that directly: what following them has left after the cost of following them, on the trades that reached a result.

You can’t watch Polymarket all day

Good trades happen around the clock. You’re asleep, at work, or just not looking. By the time you see a trade worth copying, it’s too late.

Trader Bots run 24/7. Pick a trader, set your rules. The bot copies their qualifying trades automatically.

Blind copying is a bad idea

Most copy trading tools mirror everything a wallet does. Winners, experiments, mistakes. No filter, no context, no control.

Every trade on Polycopy shows the trader’s data. You decide what to copy. A Trader Bot applies your filters to every trade before it executes.

Overall stats hide the real signal

A trader with a 60% win rate sounds decent. But that number doesn’t tell you whether they’re good at politics trades, NBA props, or crypto. It’s an average that hides the variance.

Trader profiles break down performance by market type, bet structure, and price range. You see where someone’s edge actually lives.

What is PolyInsider?

PolyInsider is a real-time analytics dashboard for Polymarket, the largest prediction market. It watches the live trade feed and shows you what moved, how strong the conviction looks, and where to act next, without you sitting there reading the chain yourself.

The core is whale tracking. Every large bet on Polymarket is surfaced the moment it prints, with the trader’s true position size pulled from on-chain data so the number is accurate rather than a partial fill. Alongside whale alerts, PolyInsider flags fresh wallets placing their first bet on a market, matches breaking news to the markets it moves, and maps geo-tagged markets on a live 3D globe.

Every market and every trader has its own page with live prices, order flow, and profit and loss history. PolyInsider is free, independent, and built for traders who want an edge on Polymarket prediction markets.

Frequently asked questions

What is PolyInsider?

PolyInsider is a real-time analytics dashboard for Polymarket prediction markets. It tracks whale trades, fresh wallet activity, news matched to live markets, and visualizes geo-tagged markets on a 3D globe.

How are whale alerts detected?

Whale alerts surface buy trades above $5,000 from any wallet on Polymarket, streamed in real time via the Polymarket WebSocket feed and reconciled against on-chain positions for accurate sizing.

What are fresh trades?

Fresh trades are entries from wallets making their first significant bet on a market, surfacing early conviction before whales pile in.

Is PolyInsider free?

Yes, PolyInsider is free to use. We do not collect personal data, and outbound Polymarket links may include a referral parameter.

Is PolyInsider affiliated with Polymarket?

No, PolyInsider is an independent analytics platform and is not affiliated with Polymarket.

Which markets does PolyInsider cover?

PolyInsider covers all active Polymarket markets, including politics, sports, crypto, economics, and culture, with a dedicated page for every market and every trader.

How is PolyInsider different from the Polymarket app?

Polymarket lets you trade; PolyInsider reads the order flow for you. It surfaces whale bets, fresh-wallet entries, and news catalysts in real time so you can spot moves before they are obvious, then trade them on Polymarket.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I install PolyPulse?

To install PolyPulse:

  1. Visit the Chrome Web Store
  2. Click "Add to Chrome"
  3. Confirm the installation when prompted
  4. Open the extension by clicking its icon in your browser toolbar

How does the automatic market detection work?

PolyPulse features automatic market detection that instantly identifies active Polymarket markets. When you visit a market, it automatically scans for the market question and begins gathering relevant news and insights to deliver customized summaries.

Is my Perplexity API key safe?

Yes, your Perplexity API key is stored securely in your Chrome browser and never transmitted to our servers. PolyPulse is designed with data security as a priority - no personal data is collected or stored. Your privacy is important to us.

How accurate are the AI-powered summaries?

The AI-powered summaries use Perplexity AI to generate automated summaries and detailed insights from trusted news sources. This provides you with comprehensive analysis to make more informed trading decisions on Polymarket.

While we strive for accuracy, we cannot give a 100% guarantee on the reliability of AI-generated content. These summaries should be used as one of several tools in your research process, and important trading decisions should always be validated with multiple sources.

How often are the market summaries updated?

Market summaries are generated on-demand when you open the extension. Our efficient caching ensures fast load times and reduced API usage. You can manually refresh summaries at any time using the "Refresh Summary" button to get the latest insights.

Do I need a Perplexity account to use PolyPulse?

Yes, you need a Perplexity account to get an API key. Visit perplexity.ai/settings/api to create an account and obtain your API key. This key powers the AI-driven news analysis in PolyPulse.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I install Polyteller?
Installing Polyteller is simple. Visit the Chrome Web Store, click "Add to Chrome", and confirm the installation. The extension works with Chrome and Chromium-based browsers (version 110+) like Edge and Brave. Once installed, you'll see the Polyteller icon in your browser's extension toolbar.
How accurate are the countdown timers?
Our countdown timers are highly accurate with built-in timezone handling. They automatically: - Convert all times to your local timezone - Handle Daylight Saving Time (DST) changes - Update in real-time without page refresh - Show warnings during DST transition periods - Sync with Polymarket's servers for precision
How does Privacy Mode work?
Privacy Mode instantly masks your portfolio values and balances across all Polymarket tabs. To use it: - Click the Polyteller icon - Toggle Privacy Mode on/off - Changes apply immediately to all open tabs - Settings persist between browser sessions This is perfect for trading while sharing your screen or in public spaces.
Can I customize notification timing?
Yes! You can set multiple custom notifications for each event: - Click the Polyteller icon - Set your preferred notification times - Choose multiple time points (e.g., 1 hour, 30 mins, 5 mins before event end) - Notifications work even when browser is closed - All notifications show in your local timezone
How does Trade Safety work?
Trade Safety helps prevent accidental trades with: - Optional confirmation dialog for all trades - Keyboard shortcuts (Enter to confirm, Esc to cancel) - 3-second countdown timer on cancellation - Works across all Polymarket markets - Can be toggled on/off in settings Note: Confirmation dialogs are automatically disabled on small screens for better mobile experience.
What happens when I switch between markets?
Polyteller intelligently handles market navigation: - Auto-detects market changes - Updates countdown timers automatically when possible - Shows refresh hint when manual refresh is needed - Maintains privacy settings across all markets - Syncs notifications across browser sessions
Can't find what you're looking for?
If you couldn't find the answer to your question, our support team is here to help! Send us an email at hi@polyteller.com, and we'll get back to you as soon as possible. Please include as much detail as possible about your issue to help us assist you better.

To use it: - Click the Polyteller icon - Toggle Privacy Mode on/off - Changes apply immediately to all open tabs - Settings persist between browser sessions This is perfect for trading while sharing your screen or in public spaces.
Can I customize notification timing?
Yes! You can set multiple custom notifications for each event: - Click the Polyteller icon - Set your preferred notification times - Choose multiple time points (e.g., 1 hour, 30 mins, 5 mins before event end) - Notifications work even when browser is closed - All notifications show in your local timezone
How does Trade Safety work?
Trade Safety helps prevent accidental trades with: - Optional confirmation dialog for all trades - Keyboard shortcuts (Enter to confirm, Esc to cancel) - 3-second countdown timer on cancellation - Works across all Polymarket markets - Can be toggled on/off in settings Note: Confirmation dialogs are automatically disabled on small screens for better mobile experience.
What happens when I switch between markets?
Polyteller intelligently handles market navigation: - Auto-detects market changes - Updates countdown timers automatically when possible - Shows refresh hint when manual refresh is needed - Maintains privacy settings across all markets - Syncs notifications across browser sessions
Can't find what you're looking for?
If you couldn't find the answer to your question, our support team is here to help! Send us an email at hi@polyteller.com, and we'll get back to you as soon as possible. Please include as much detail as possible about your issue to help us assist you better.

body:
olytrack affiliated with Polymarket?

No. Polytrack is an independent dashboard for monitoring and analyzing Polymarket activity. It is not an exchange, broker, or first-party Polymarket application.

Does Polytrack give financial advice or trade automatically?

No. Polytrack does not place trades, manage funds, or tell you what to buy. Severity labels, including "insider" language, are heuristic screens - most flagged trades are not insider trading. See our Terms of Service for the full risk disclosure.

How do Telegram alerts work?

You connect your own Telegram bot token and chat ID, then choose HIGH severity alerts, watched-wallet alerts, or both.

What makes a trade HIGH severity?

Severity considers trade size, short-window volume, volume spikes, price movement, sensitive market categories, coordinated wallets, one-direction flow, accumulation, new wallets, and repeat flagged wallet activity.

Can I follow specific wallets?

Yes. Add any valid Polymarket wallet to your watchlist, label it if you want, and monitor its recent trades separately from the main feed.

How quickly can I start?

Create an account, complete checkout, and open the dashboard. Telegram is optional and can be connected from settings later.

Can I cancel?

The one-time crypto payment is a lifetime purchase, so there is nothing to cancel. A weekly or yearly card subscription can be canceled anytime; cancelling stops future renewals but does not refund the current period.
